output.title: AWS serverless orders
output.description: API Gateway and Lambda write orders to DynamoDB; its stream feeds EventBridge rules that fan out to a Step Functions payment workflow, an isolated fulfillment queue, an archive queue and SNS notifications, with a scheduled reconciliation.

simulations.title: Flash sale: 300 orders/s
simulations.description: Steady traffic jumps to 300 orders a second for three seconds; Lambda scales out and nothing queues for long.

action.text: Every write to the orders table lands on its stream. One Lambda turns stream records into EventBridge events; rules route them by type. Each dot is 10 orders.
The flash sale peaks at 300 orders a second. API Gateway and Lambda scale out; there are no servers to add.
The payment workflow writes PAID back to the table. That change comes round the stream as OrderPaid, which the other two rules pick up.

expectations.label: Each order is written twice: placed, then paid

simulations.title: 3PL outage and DLQ redrive
simulations.description: The warehouse API fails for five seconds; SQS retries after a visibility timeout, parks failures in the DLQ, and an operator redrives them.

action.text: The 3PL's API is down. Each shipment request fails, becomes visible again after the timeout, and is retried.
After three receives, SQS moves the message to the dead-letter queue. Payments and receipts are unaffected.
The 3PL is back, so an operator redrives the DLQ. Every parked shipment goes through.

expectations.label: The DLQ is empty after the redrive

simulations.title: Fulfillment Lambda is throttled
simulations.description: Reserved concurrency for RequestShipment drops to one. Its queue grows while payments, the archive and receipts carry on; when concurrency is restored, the backlog drains.

action.text: Each EventBridge rule feeds its own queue, so one slow consumer can't hold up the others.
RequestShipment is throttled to one concurrent execution. Its queue grows; the archive and receipts are unaffected.
Reserved concurrency is restored and fulfillment catches up.
